text:
maya.design: Quick design nit — the confirmation modal for stopping a dedicated pool has a secondary link reading 'Learn more about consequences'. Feels long and ambiguous when announced by screen readers. Proposing alternatives. oliver.pm: yep saw that. copy feels verbose. do we even need 'about consequences'? there should be context in the modal body. samir.eng: accessibility + keyboard flow question: screen reader will read the link text in isolation if it's focused. 'Learn more about consequences' might be OK but it's long. Short, descriptive link text is ideal. jess.prod: agree with both. also product concern: if someone clicks the link we should surface the short doc (2-3 bullets). make sure we track click as conversion. :eyes: maya.design: my proposed microcopy options (shortlist): - Option A: 'Learn more' (with aria-describedby pointing to the paragraph explaining rollback/cost) - Option B: 'Rollout & rollback details' - Option C: 'What happens when you stop a pool' Pick one and I'll update. oliver.pm: I lean Option C for clarity. But it might be long visually. Option A + aria-describedby seems cleanest and compact. samir.eng: technical call: if we go with 'Learn more', we must add aria-label that includes context for screen readers, or link should be adjacent to the explanatory paragraph with aria-describedby referencing the paragraph id. Example: ```html

Stopping this pool will evict all in-flight jobs and may extend job completion times. Jobs are attempted to be drained over 5 minutes.

Learn more ``` This keeps the visual copy short but keeps screen reader context. a11y-bot: Accessibility check: WCAG recommend link text to make sense out of context. If you add aria-describedby it meets the requirement. Also ensure focus order: Link should come after body text, before cancel/confirm buttons. jess.prod: thumbs up on aria-describedby approach. product note: we should A/B test 'Learn more' vs 'What happens when you stop a pool' for support ticket reduction. low effort: track outbound clicks and subsequent support flow. maya.design: updated CTA suggestion: Primary button text: 'Stop pool' (danger style), Secondary link: 'Learn more' with aria-describedby="#stop-info". Inline helper text in modal body to summarise immediate customer impact (one-liner). I'll push a tiny mock into Figma. oliver.pm: sounds good. one more nit: the confirm button should include the pool name? e.g., 'Stop pool — prod-gpu-1' to reduce accidental stops. what do you think? samir.eng: adding resource name is fine but watch truncation on mobile. implementation-wise we can set title attr and visually show shortened name. a11y-bot: minor: ensure confirm button has aria-describedby as well if you include extra cautionary text. Also color contrast and focus ring checks for danger button. maya.design: thanks all — I'll update the modal copy and post the Figma link when ready. tagging @oliver.pm for product review once it's in figma. :sparkles:
